title: Nominal Cardiac Rhythm & Rate
actions: Maintain planned daily cardiovascular countermeasure routine (T2 treadmill / cycle ergometer).
Continue standard daily hydration protocol of 2.0 to 2.5 L with electrolyte balance.
Log scheduled resting telemetry reading during evening post-exercise debrief.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if heart rate remains nominal but you experience unexpected palpitations, chest tightness, or lightheadedness.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Sub-Nominal Resting Heart Rate Variance
actions: Pause intense physical countermeasure workloads for the next 2 hours.
Drink 500 mL of oral electrolyte solution to address microgravity hypovolemia.
Check telemetry sensor contact and lead attachment on the bio-harness.
Re-measure resting heart rate after 2 hours of quiet station activities.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if resting heart rate exceeds 100 BPM for two consecutive checks or is accompanied by dizziness.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Critical Cardiac Telemetry Alert
actions: Cease all EVA preparations, treadmill training, and strenuous physical activities immediately.
Adopt a neutral recumbent microgravity rest posture with tethered support.
Notify crew medical officer (CMO) and standby for flight surgeon audio uplink.
Keep 12-lead ECG bio-harness streaming continuous telemetry to MCC ground station.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately via Space-to-Ground Audio Channel B or CapCom priority line.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Nominal Arterial Perfusion
actions: Continue standard orbital dietary sodium intake (1.5–2.3 g/day).
Perform scheduled lower-body negative pressure (LBNP) maintenance if in mission rotation.
Record next blood pressure measurement at nominal morning check-in.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if sudden orthostatic visual narrowing or headache develops despite nominal readings.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Elevated or Depressed Blood Pressure Variance
actions: Review recent sodium and caffeine intake from station food rations.
Perform 15 minutes of lower-body muscle tensing and calf compression exercises.
Ensure proper cuff placement over the brachial artery at heart level.
Re-measure blood pressure in 4 hours while seated quietly for 5 minutes.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if systolic pressure remains above 135 mmHg or below 90 mmHg across two consecutive readings.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Severe Hemodynamic Pressure Deviation
actions: Rest immediately in sleep quarters with minimal sensory and auditory stimulation.
Have crewmate prepare manual sphygmomanometer from Crew Medical Pack for verification.
Avoid rapid translational movements across habitat modules to prevent syncope.
Establish direct private medical conference (PMC) with MCC Flight Surgeon.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Systolic ≥ 141 mmHg or ≤ 84 mmHg indicates acute perfusion risk.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Balanced Metabolic Glucose Levels
actions: Follow scheduled balanced macronutrient meal packs (50% carb, 30% fat, 20% protein).
Keep standard post-exercise carbohydrate replenishment snacks timed within 45 minutes.
Log regular check-in during morning pre-work routine.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if experiencing symptoms of shakiness, extreme thirst, or sweating.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Moderate Glycemic Departure
actions: Consume a complex carbohydrate snack with 250 mL water if reading is sub-nominal.
If elevated, delay high-sugar snack pouches and emphasize lean protein and fiber.
Verify glucometer calibration test strip lot number with station inventory.
Re-measure blood glucose level in 2 hours.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if blood sugar is <65 mg/dL with tremor or >160 mg/dL with persistent nausea.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Critical Glucose Imbalance Alert
actions: If hypoglycemic (<60 mg/dL), consume emergency oral glucose gel pouch immediately.
If severely hyperglycemic (>180 mg/dL), drink water continuously and check for ketones if kit available.
Crew Medical Officer must assist with repeat capillary blood verification.
Request Flight Surgeon telemetry consult for insulin or glucose countermeasure protocol.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately via mission audio loop: severe glycemic crisis compromises EVA and flight safety.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Nominal Core Thermoregulation
actions: Keep habitability module ventilation ducts unobstructed to ensure convective air movement.
Wear appropriate thermal clothing layers during low-activity sleep shifts.
Log core telemetry during scheduled daily medical check-in.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if chills, feverish sensation, or localized heat discomfort occur.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Elevated Microgravity Core Temperature
actions: Adjust personal air-diffuser velocity in work compartment to maximize evaporative cooling.
Remove heavy thermal layers and apply cool damp wipes to forehead and neck.
Drink 400 mL chilled electrolyte water to support core cooling.
Re-measure core body temperature in 2 hours.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if core temperature exceeds 37.8°C or fails to drop after 2 hours of cooling.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Hyperthermia or Hypothermia Warning
actions: Cease all physical exertion and remove any restrictive pressure or exercise garments.
Access Crew Medical Pack antipyretic protocol under CMO supervision.
Verify ECLSS cabin environmental temperature and humidity readings with ground control.
Initiate immediate Flight Surgeon voice consult for thermal regulation intervention.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Core temperature ≥ 38.0°C indicates systemic infection or severe thermoregulatory failure.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Adequate Restorative Sleep Window
actions: Maintain circadian sleep berth lighting schedule (dimmed blue spectrum 1 hour before sleep).
Keep sleep station earplugs and noise-canceling headsets accessible during ventilation cycles.
Aim for uninterrupted 8.0-hour sleep opportunity each orbital day.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if unrefreshing sleep or daytime sleepiness persists for more than 3 days.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Sub-Optimal Rest Deficit
actions: Schedule a 20 to 30-minute power rest period in private sleep station before afternoon shift.
Limit high-caffeine rations during the 6 hours preceding the next sleep window.
Verify sleep berth ventilation fan speed and carbon dioxide scrubbing levels.
Re-evaluate cumulative sleep debt after tomorrow's wake-up cycle.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if cumulative sleep duration drops below 11 hours across two consecutive days.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Critical Sleep Deprivation & Cognitive Risk
actions: Stand down from robotic arm teleoperation, docking operations, and critical valve maneuvering.
Complete brief cognitive readiness battery on station tablet.
Review station sleep aid medications (melatonin / zolpidem) with Flight Surgeon.
Request schedule adjustment from Mission Planning Lead to protect recovery sleep block.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Sleep < 5.0 hours triggers mandatory flight rule fatigue review.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: High Cognitive Morale & Operational Readiness
actions: Participate in daily communal crew meal and recreational downtime.
Utilize station Cupola / Earth observation window time for mental restoration.
Continue regular family audio/video communication conferences as scheduled.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon or behavioral health specialist whenever you feel mounting psychological strain.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Operational Stress or Sensory Fatigue
actions: Engage in 20 minutes of guided audio meditation or binaural relaxation in private quarters.
Schedule non-operational personal conference with family or ground support team.
Review workload timeline with Commander to rebalance task allocation.
Re-evaluate behavioral state at the next shift handover.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon or Behavioral Health and Performance (BHP) team if feelings of isolation or irritability persist.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Severe Behavioral Strain or Disorientation Alert
actions: Step back from solitary or safety-critical mission console operations.
Notify Mission Commander or Crew Medical Officer for peer support.
Transfer to low-stimulus environment with dim ambient lighting in Crew Quarters.
Initiate confidential Private Psychological Conference (PPC) with NASA BHP team.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Acute disorientation or psychological crisis requires immediate mission support.
source: To be confirmed by research team

title: Nominal Systolic Pressure
actions: Maintain standard orbital dietary sodium and hydration routine.
Log resting blood pressure during nominal morning check-in.
Continue standard daily countermeasure exercises.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if experiencing sudden visual changes, headache, or dizziness despite nominal readings.

title: Sub-nominal / Elevated Systolic Pressure
actions: Rest seated quietly for 10 minutes with arm at heart level.
Drink 400 mL oral electrolyte solution to support intravascular volume.
Check cuff placement on bare upper arm and repeat measurement in 2 hours.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if systolic pressure remains in warning band across two consecutive readings.

title: Critical Systolic Hypertensive / Hypotensive Crisis
actions: Cease all strenuous operations and recline in neutral microgravity posture.
Notify Crew Medical Officer and verify reading with manual sphygmomanometer.
Standby for direct Flight Surgeon voice uplink.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Systolic pressure <= 90 or > 180 mmHg represents an acute perfusion emergency.

title: Nominal Diastolic Pressure
actions: Continue standard cardiovascular conditioning routine.
Maintain adequate fluid intake of 2.0 to 2.5 L daily.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if accompanied by chest discomfort or lightheadedness.

title: Diastolic Pressure Departure
actions: Review recent caffeine and sodium intake.
Perform 15 minutes of lower-body muscle activation.
Re-measure in 2 hours after 5 minutes of seated rest.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if diastolic pressure remains elevated above 80 mmHg across multiple checks.

title: Severe Diastolic Crisis (>120 mmHg)
actions: Rest in quiet sleep quarters immediately.
Have CMO verify readings on alternate arm.
Prepare emergency cardiovascular diagnostic kit.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Diastolic pressure > 120 mmHg requires urgent medical intervention.

title: Nominal Respiration Rate
actions: Breathing rate 12-20 breaths/min is optimal.
Continue routine morning vital check-in.
Ensure crew quarters ventilation diffusers are unobstructed.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if shortness of breath occurs at rest.

title: Respiratory Variance Advisory
actions: Check vehicle cabin CO2 and O2 telemetry displays.
Sit comfortably and practice controlled diaphragmatic breathing for 5 minutes.
Re-measure resting breathing rate in 1 hour.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if breathing rate remains >= 21 or <= 11 breaths/min after rest.

title: Critical Respiratory Distress Alert
actions: Don emergency cabin breathing mask or portable O2 supply if hypoxia suspected.
Cease all physical exertion and notify Crew Medical Officer immediately.
Have crewmate check cabin atmospheric scrubbers for toxic contaminants.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Breathing rate <= 8 or >= 25 breaths/min indicates severe respiratory failure or hypercapnia.

title: Optimal Blood Oxygen Saturation
actions: Blood oxygen saturation (>=96%) is optimal for spaceflight operations.
Maintain standard cabin atmosphere monitoring.
Log reading before and after any planned extravehicular activity (EVA).
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if SpO2 drops below 96% during routine activities.

title: Mild Hypoxemia Warning (92-95%)
actions: Warm hands and re-seat pulse oximeter sensor on alternate finger.
Check vehicle environmental ECLSS oxygen partial pressure reading.
Take deep rhythmic breaths and re-test in 15 minutes.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if SpO2 fails to rise above 95% after sensor repositioning.

title: Critical Hypoxia Alert (<=91%)
actions: Immediately connect to spacecraft emergency medical oxygen mask.
Cease all physical workload and maintain passive resting posture.
Crew Medical Officer must confirm reading and monitor mental clarity.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: SpO2 <= 91% represents an acute hypoxemia emergency in spaceflight.

title: Nominal Fasting Blood Sugar
actions: Fasting glucose of 70-99 mg/dL is within healthy metabolic bounds.
Maintain planned nutritional macro balance.
Continue weekly or team-scheduled glucose logging.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if experiencing unexplained dizziness, sweating, or shakiness.

title: Mild Glycemic Variance
actions: If low (54-69 mg/dL), consume a 15 g carbohydrate snack pouch.
If elevated (100-125 mg/dL), review recent diet logs and ensure adequate hydration.
Verify glucometer strip code and re-test in 2 hours.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if persistent fasting glucose exceeds 120 mg/dL across three readings.

title: Severe Glycemic Crisis (<54 or >=126 mg/dL)
actions: If <54 mg/dL (severe hypoglycemia), ingest fast-acting glucose gel immediately.
If >=126 mg/dL, hydrate continuously with water and assess for ketones.
Have CMO verify capillary sample.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately for urgent metabolic review.
source: CDC Low Blood Sugar & Diabetes Testing

title: Adequate Restorative Sleep
actions: Logged sleep of 7+ hours meets the restorative target.
Keep circadian lighting dimmed 1 hour before sleep shift.
Ensure sleep station acoustic isolation earplugs are utilized.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if feeling chronically fatigued despite 7+ hours logged.

title: Sub-Target Sleep Warning (6-6.9h or single night <6h)
actions: Schedule a 20-30 minute restorative nap before afternoon mission shift.
Limit caffeine rations during the 6 hours preceding the next sleep window.
Check sleep quarters ventilation and carbon dioxide scrubbing.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if sleep debt accumulates across consecutive days.

title: Chronic Sleep Deprivation (3 Consecutive Nights <6h)
actions: Stand down from high-risk robotics, docking, and EVA operations.
Complete brief cognitive readiness assessment on station tablet.
Review sleep aid protocols (melatonin) with Flight Surgeon.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: 3 nights under 6 hours triggers mandatory fatigue protocol.

title: Nominal Cabin CO2 Level (<=3.0 mmHg)
actions: Cabin CO2 <= 3.0 mmHg meets NASA-STD-3001 operational standards.
Maintain regular airflow scrubber inspections.
Report any localized air pocket stagnation in crew quarters.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if experiencing unexplained frontal headaches or visual disturbance.

title: Elevated Cabin CO2 Warning (3.1-4.5 mmHg)
actions: Inspect cabin air circulation fans and increase airflow mixing in crew quarters.
Verify Carbon Dioxide Removal Assembly (CDRA) telemetry status.
Monitor crew members for headache, irritability, or drowsiness.
Re-check cabin CO2 sensor in 1 hour.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if headache develops or cabin CO2 remains above 3.5 mmHg.

title: Dangerous Hypercapnia Risk (>4.5 mmHg)
actions: Switch life support to backup CO2 scrubbing beds immediately.
Don emergency breathing masks if symptoms of severe headache, nausea, or confusion occur.
Notify Capcom and Flight Surgeon console on primary Space-to-Ground loop.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon and Mission Control immediately: Cabin CO2 > 4.5 mmHg impairs cognitive and operational flight safety.

title: Career Radiation Exposure Nominal (<300 mSv)
actions: Career accumulated dose is within the safe lower tier (<300 mSv).
Wear personal dosimeter continuously during all flight duties.
Log daily incremental dosimeter readings during evening debrief.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if dosimeter alarms or unusual solar particle warnings sound.

title: Career Radiation Advisory (300-599 mSv)
actions: 50% or more of career lifetime limit reached.
Prioritize time in well-shielded habitat modules (storm shelters).
Minimize scheduled extravehicular activities to critical maintenance only.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Consult Flight Surgeon for career exposure pacing and mission dosimetric projection.
source: NASA OCHMO TB-020 / Team Choice 50% Limit

title: Career Radiation Limit Reached (>=600 mSv)
actions: Cease all unshielded activities immediately and retreat to storm shelter.
Full dosimetric sensor calibration and blood lymphocyte count check.
Convene mandatory Flight Surgeon and Radiation Health Officer review.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Career dose >= 600 mSv triggers mandatory mission flight termination rules. Note: SPE limit is 250 mSv single event.

title: Exercise Countermeasure Complete (>=120 min)
actions: Completed full 2.0-hour daily exercise countermeasure.
Maintain hydration and electrolyte recovery.
Preserves bone mineral density and cardiovascular capacity in zero-g.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if joint pain, muscle strain, or acute fatigue occurs during exercise.
source: JAXA / NASA HRP Bone Remodeling Model

title: Sub-Target Exercise Duration (60-119 min or single day <60 min)
actions: Schedule a supplemental 30-minute cycle ergometer or ARED session tomorrow.
Perform active stretching in crew quarters.
Review daily task schedule to ensure 2 hours protected countermeasure time.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact flight surgeon if physical pain or mission constraints prevent exercise.

title: Severe Deconditioning Risk (2 Consecutive Days <60 min)
actions: Immediately schedule mandatory countermeasure session.
Assess for musculoskeletal injury, illness, or equipment failure.
Consult Flight Surgeon and ASCR (Astronaut Strength, Conditioning, and Rehabilitation) coach.
whenToContactFlightSurgeon: Contact Flight Surgeon immediately: Two days under 60 min triggers accelerated bone/muscle loss protocol.
